statement: At a bakery, the number of loaves baked in $h$ hours is $n(h) = 45h + 10$, and the cost, in dollars, of baking $n$ loaves is $C(n) = 0.8n + 60$. What is the value of $C\big(n(4)\big)$?

choices.misconception: I found $n(4) = 190$ and multiplied by $0.8$, but I forgot to add the fixed cost of $60$.
I added $n(4) = 190$ and $C(4) = 63.2$ instead of putting $n(4)$ into $C$.
I worked in the wrong order and put $C(4) = 63.2$ into $n$, which gives $n\big(C(4)\big)$ instead of $C\big(n(4)\big)$.

hints: Work from the inside out: find $n(4)$ first.
$n(4)$ is the number of loaves baked in $4$ hours. Use that number as the input to $C$.

solutions.reliable: First, $n(4) = 45 \cdot 4 + 10 = 190$ loaves. Then $C(190) = 0.8 \cdot 190 + 60 = 152 + 60 = 212$. So $C\big(n(4)\big) = 212$, the cost in dollars of baking for $4$ hours.
